seed: Somebody drawing an icon outline with the Pen stops before the last point and presses Return. Until now that run was open for good and could never be filled. This walk draws three corners of a triangle with the last run missing, picks the one row, and checks that the command is offered at all, that it calls itself Close Path rather than Turn Into Path, that it says the gap in points before it does anything, that it lays a straight run between the two ends without moving either, that the Fill row turns up afterwards, that one undo puts the open line back, and that an outline whose points are in a line is refused out loud instead.

steps.note: two sides of a triangle, drawn with the Pen and finished with Return. It LOOKS like a shape and is nothing of the kind: no inside, no Fill row on the panel, nothing to paint

THE POINT: before this, one open path picked on its own offered nothing at all. The row is here now and it reads 'Close Path…' rather than 'Turn Into Path…', because this is not a shape and there is nothing to join it to

the question reads 'Close this path?' and says a straight run joins its two ends, how far apart they are in points, that neither end moves, and that the outline closes so you can paint inside it. The button says Close Path. Nothing has changed yet

THE POINT: the bottom run is there and it is straight, and both ends are exactly where they were. Compare doc-1-open with doc-4-closed: nothing else moved. The line under the canvas says it closed and where the inside now is
closing is ONE step: a single undo takes the run away and the outline is open again, wearing the same colour and line it always had

THE OTHER HALF OF THE PROMISE: three points in a row. Closing them up would leave a layer painting no pixels, so it refuses. The command is still offered, because a row dimmed for this teaches nobody anything, and the refusal is the Pen's own sentence: these points are in a line, so joining them up has no inside
